Executive Summary

  • Interest rate tightening: A net 43.8% of Slovak firms reported tighter interest rates in wave 39, up 38.3 pp from net 5.5%, exceeding the EA's net 40.0% and Germany's net 42.5%.
  • Present-future divergence: Slovak turnover expectations fell to a net 6.75% against the euro area's rising net 25.88%, a 19 pp gap, even as current turnover losses narrowed.
  • Credit line stress persists: The Slovak credit line gap widened to +15.3pp as need rose, while the bank loan gap improved to -6.0pp and trade credit swung to -1.7pp.
  • Margin compression: Labour costs rose for a net 79% of Slovak firms, 20 pp above the euro area's net 59%, while a net 34% still reported declining profits.

Financing Conditions

Interest rate tightening for Slovak firms rose sharply to a net 43.8%

Changes in Terms and Conditions of Bank Financing (Q10)

  • A net 43.8% of Slovak firms (n=76) reported tighter interest rates in wave 39, rising 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% in wave 38, exceeding the EA's net 40.0% and Germany's net 42.5%.
  • Credit line and loan size availability tightened further, with a net 12.4% of Slovak firms (n=74) reporting a reduction, up 6.3 pp from net 6.1% in wave 38.
  • Loan maturity tightened for a net 11.6% of Slovak firms (n=76), well above the EA's net 4.4% and Germany's net 3.4%.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

ⓘ SQL — bank_loan_terms.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Chart 1: Changes in terms and conditions of bank financing (Q10)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Austria (AT), Germany (DE)
-- All firm sizes combined (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves
--
-- net_balance_wtd: positive = net tightening (adverse for firms)
--                 negative = net easing (favourable for firms)
-- Sub-items:
--   a = Level of interest rates
--   b = Non-interest financing costs (charges, fees, commissions)
--   c = Available size of loan or credit line
--   d = Available maturity of the loan
--   e = Collateral requirements
--   f = Other terms (guarantees, covenants, procedures)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q10'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.pct_unchanged_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions f
WHERE f.question_id = 'q10'
  AND f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Credit line stress persists as bank loan and trade credit conditions ease

Financing Need vs Availability Gap (Q5/Q9)

  • The Slovak credit line gap widened to +15.3pp (n=270) from +14.8pp in the previous wave, driven by need rising to a net +15.2pp, leaving Slovak firms 1.3pp more stressed than the euro area.
  • The Slovak bank loan gap improved to -6.0pp (n=214) from -4.0pp, as availability rose to a net +5.6pp from +1.4pp — placing Slovak firms 8.8pp less stressed than the euro area's +2.8pp.
  • The Slovak trade credit gap swung to -1.7pp (n=180) from +6.3pp, as need fell to a net -3.4pp from +7.1pp, leaving Slovak firms 12.7pp less stressed than the euro area.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

ⓘ SQL — financing_gap.sql (cited column: financing_gap_wtd)
-- Financing need vs availability gap (Q5/Q9) from mart_safe__financing_conditions
-- financing_gap_wtd = Q5 net balance (need) minus Q9 net balance (availability)
-- Positive gap = need exceeds availability (adverse for firms)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- Returns two result sets unioned:
--   type='main'  — bank loans (sub_item='a') for SK/EA/DE — used for the main grouped-bar chart
--   type='sk_all' — all major instruments for SK only — used for the SK instrument breakdown chart

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
),

q5 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, survey_period_label, country_code, sub_item, sub_item_label,
           net_balance_wtd AS need_nb, n_respondents AS n_respondents_need
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q5'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

q9 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, country_code, sub_item,
           net_balance_wtd        AS availability_nb,
           financing_gap_wtd,
           n_respondents          AS n_respondents_avail
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

joined AS (
    SELECT
        q5.wave_number,
        q5.survey_period_label,
        q5.country_code,
        q5.sub_item,
        q5.sub_item_label,
        q5.need_nb,
        q9.availability_nb,
        q9.financing_gap_wtd,
        q5.n_respondents_need,
        q9.n_respondents_avail
    FROM q5
    JOIN q9 USING (wave_number, country_code, sub_item)
)

-- Main chart: bank loans (a), credit lines (f), trade credit (b) for SK/EA/DE
SELECT *, 'main' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE sub_item IN ('a', 'f', 'b')

UNION ALL

-- SK instrument breakdown: all instruments for Slovakia only
SELECT *, 'sk_all' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE country_code = 'SK'
  AND sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'f', 'g', 'h')

ORDER BY chart_type, sub_item, country_code, wave_number

Slovak firms' discouragement rate fell below euro area level in wave 39

Bank Loan Applications and Access Conditions (Q7A/Q7B)

  • The share of Slovak firms (n=131) that did not apply for bank loans fearing rejection fell from 5.76% (wave 38) to 1.81% (wave 39), below the EA's 2.37% (n=3,607).
  • Slovak firms' bank loan application rate remained well below the EA average (n=3,607), with the rejection rate too sparse to permit a reliable financing gap estimate for Slovakia.
  • The EA financing gap eased from 4.54% (wave 38) to 3.48% (n=3,607) in wave 39, as both EA discouragement and rejection rates declined.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

🤖 This section includes data retrieved by an AI agent querying the SAFE database directly during report generation.

ⓘ SQL — loan_applications.sql (cited column: financing_gap_wtd)
-- Q7A/Q7B: Bank loan applications, discouragement, rejection and financing gap
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), bank loans (sub_item='a'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- financing_gap_wtd = discouragement + rejection share (ECB headline access indicator)
-- Higher financing_gap = worse access to bank loans

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__loan_applications
    WHERE sub_item = 'a'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.application_rate_wtd,
    f.discouragement_rate_wtd,
    f.rejection_rate_wtd,
    f.financing_gap_wtd,
    f.n_total AS n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__loan_applications f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.sub_item = 'a'
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms' bank loan availability expectations diverged from improving EA trend

Expected Availability of External Financing (Q23)

  • A net 6% of Slovak firms (n=104) expected bank loan availability to deteriorate, worsening 1.3 pp from the previous wave, while EA firms' expectations improved 1.5 pp to a net 2% expecting deterioration (n=2803).
  • Slovak trade credit expectations improved by 4.0 pp to a net 6% expecting deterioration (n=90), reversing the prior wave's pessimism, even as EA trade credit expectations edged 1.0 pp more adverse.
  • Slovak credit line availability expectations improved by 3.2 pp to a net 4% expecting deterioration (n=136), narrowing the gap with the EA's net 2%, though both remained in negative territory.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — availability_expectations.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q23: Expected availability of external financing over the next quarter
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % expecting improvement minus % expecting deterioration
-- Positive = more firms expect availability to IMPROVE (FAVOURABLE)
-- Negative = more firms expect availability to DETERIORATE (ADVERSE)
--
-- Sub-items (matching Q5/Q9 instruments):
--   b = Bank loans
--   d = Trade credit
--   g = Credit lines and bank overdraft

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improve_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorate_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Fixed investment financing rose among Slovak firms, surpassing the euro area share

Purpose of Financing (Q6A)

  • Fixed investment citations rose from 34.2% to 40.7% among Slovak firms (n=242), up 6.5 pp from the previous wave and above the EA's 38.4%.
  • Inventory and working capital remained the dominant financing purpose for Slovak firms at 57.0% (n=242), 16.2 pp above the EA's 40.8%.
  • Refinancing or paying off obligations declined from 21.5% to 17.0% among Slovak firms (n=241), converging toward the EA's 15.8%.
ⓘ SQL — financing_purpose.sql (cited column: pct_cited_wtd)
-- Q6A: Purpose of financing (multi-select)
-- pct_cited_wtd = % of firms citing each purpose (can sum > 100% as multi-select)
-- purposes: 1=Fixed investment, 2=Inventory/working capital, 3=Hiring/training,
--           4=New products/services, 5=Refinancing, 6=Other
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.purpose_id,
    f.purpose_label,
    f.pct_cited_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.purpose_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Bank credit willingness stable but economic outlook weighs on Slovak firms

Factors Affecting Access to External Financing (Q11)

  • A net 7.8% of Slovak firms (n=310) reported that banks' willingness to provide credit improved, unchanged from the previous wave and above the EA's net 5.6%.
  • A net 51.6% of Slovak firms (n=472) reported that the general economic outlook deteriorated, worsening by 7.2 pp from wave 38 and 22.2 pp below the EA's net 29.4%.
  • A net 21.2% of Slovak firms (n=310) reported deterioration in access to public financial support, improving from a net 33.8% in the previous wave, compared with the EA's net 13.6%.
ⓘ SQL — financing_factors.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q11: Self-assessed factors affecting availability of external financing
-- Net balance = % reporting improvement minus % reporting deterioration
-- Positive = factor improving (favourable for financing access)
-- Negative = factor deteriorating (adverse / potential credit supply constraint)
--
-- Key sub-items for credit supply analysis:
--   f = Willingness of banks to provide credit  (direct bank supply signal)
--   a = General economic outlook                (macro drag on supply)
--   b = Access to public financial support      (policy/guarantee channel)
--
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.sub_item IN ('f', 'a', 'b')
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Economic Situation of Firms

Slovak turnover improved but remained negative, profit gap versus EA persists

Business Situation Indicators (Q2)

  • A net 13% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported falling turnover in wave 39, improving 13 pp from the previous wave's net 26% decline, while the EA posted a net 8% increase.
  • A net 34% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported declining profits, improving 5 pp from the previous wave's net 40% decline, versus a net 15% decline across the euro area.
  • Labour costs rose for a net 79% of Slovak firms (n=242), easing 5 pp from the previous wave but remaining 20 pp above the euro area's net 59%.
ⓘ SQL — business_situation.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q2: Business situation indicators (turnover, labour costs, profit, investment, employees)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- sub_items: a=Turnover, b=Labour costs, e=Profit, g=Investment, i=Employees
-- Sign: positive = indicator rising; labour costs positive = costs rising (adverse)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_increased_wtd,
    f.pct_decreased_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak turnover expectations diverge from rising euro area optimism

Expected Changes in Turnover and Investment (Q26)

  • Slovak firms' turnover expectations fell to a net 6.75% (n=228), down 14.15 pp from two waves earlier, against the euro area's net 25.88% (n=5,266) — a gap of 19 pp.
  • Slovak fixed investment expectations rose to a net 14.67% (n=228), up 3.88 pp from two waves earlier, outpacing the euro area's net 9.45%, which itself declined 3.13 pp.
  • Euro area and German turnover expectations both improved from two waves earlier, to net 25.88% and 19.08% respectively, underscoring Slovakia's divergent trajectory.

‡ This question is not fielded every quarter — consecutive points on this chart may be more than one quarter apart. See point labels for the actual survey period.

-- Q26: Expected changes in turnover and investments over the next two quarters
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)

-- net_balance_wtd: positive = more firms expect increase (FAVOURABLE)
--                 negative = more firms expect decrease (ADVERSE)

  AND f.firm_size = 'all'

Slovak firms face persistent margin compression as input costs dwarf selling prices

Price, Wage and Employment Expectations (Q31/Q34)

  • Slovak firms expected production input prices to rise by 7.33% (n=224) over the next 12 months, 1.98 pp above the EA's 5.35%, despite easing 0.98 pp from wave 38's 8.31%.
  • Average selling price expectations stood at 3.75% (n=222) in Slovakia — above the EA's 3.27% — leaving a 3.58 pp gap between anticipated cost increases and price pass-through capacity.
  • Slovak firms anticipated average wage growth of 4.12% (n=233), 1.52 pp above the EA's 2.60%, adding further pressure on operating margins alongside elevated input cost expectations.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_quantitative.sql (cited column: mean_wtd)
-- Q31/Q34: Quantitative expectations — inflation rate (Q31) and expected % changes
-- in selling prices, input costs, wages, employment (Q34).
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- mean_wtd: weighted mean expected % change (NOT a net balance)
-- Positive = firms expect an increase; negative = firms expect a decrease.
--
-- Sub-items:
--   Q31_a = Expected inflation rate in 12 months
--   Q34_a = Average selling price of products/services
--   Q34_b = Average prices of production inputs (non-labour)
--   Q34_c = Average wage of employees
--   Q34_d = Number of employees
--
-- panel_id = question_id || '_' || sub_item to disambiguate Q31/Q34 sub_item 'a'

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q34'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.question_id,
    f.sub_item,
    f.question_id || '_' || f.sub_item                          AS panel_id,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.mean_wtd,
    f.p25_unwtd,
    f.median_unwtd,
    f.p75_unwtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id IN ('q31', 'q34')
  AND f.sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'c', 'd')
  AND f.mean_wtd IS NOT NULL
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.question_id, f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms see upside inflation risks above euro area average

Inflation Risk Outlook (Q33)

  • A net 61% of Slovak firms (n=242) saw upside risks to five-year inflation, 7 pp above the EA's net 54% (n=5,087), the widest divergence across the three economies in wave 39.
  • Slovak upside inflation risk perceptions rose mildly by 2.30 pp from a net 59% in wave 38, while the EA net balance eased marginally by 1.28 pp over the same period.
  • German firms reported a net 51% upside inflation risk, below both the EA and Slovak readings, placing Slovakia at the top of these three economies.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_risk.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q33: Main risk to 5-year inflation outlook (ordinal net balance)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % seeing upside inflation risk minus % seeing downside risk
-- Positive = more firms see inflation as a risk to the upside
-- Negative = more firms see inflation risk to the downside

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q33'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.pct_downside_wtd,
    f.pct_balanced_wtd,
    f.pct_upside_wtd,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id = 'q33'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.country_code, f.wave_number

Skilled staff shortages overtake costs as Slovak firms' top concern

Most Pressing Business Problems (Q0B)

  • Availability of skilled staff or experienced managers ranked as the most pressing problem among the seven tested for Slovak firms (n=239), scoring 6.64/10 — up 0.57 from 6.07 in the previous wave.
  • Costs of production or labour scored 6.62/10 (n=240), rising from 6.19 in the previous wave, remaining just below the EA average of 6.74/10.
  • Regulation scored 6.10/10 (n=236), easing marginally by 0.08 from the previous wave, yet remaining above the EA average of 5.87/10.
ⓘ SQL — business_problems.sql (cited column: avg_pressingness_wtd)
-- Q0B: Most pressing business problems
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.problem_id,
    f.problem_label,
    f.avg_pressingness_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.problem_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Source: ECB SAFE microdata. Net balance = % reporting increase minus % reporting decrease. Positive = tightening/rising (adverse for firms unless noted). Negative = easing/falling.
